No HOT squeezes? Zero setups? You gotta be kidding me. After weeks of squeeze after squeeze lighting up our screens, it’s like someone pulled the plug. This is what it looks like when the market goes into neutral. Everyone is stuck—no fireworks, no breakdowns, just chop. But you know what’s funny? When nothing is happening, **everything is happening.** The market's giving us an opportunity here to really step back, reset, and ask: where is the puck headed next?

So what’s the deal? With 0 HOT squeeze setups, it’s clear that risk appetite is taking a breather or recalibrating entirely. This isn’t risk-off, though. If it were, you’d see a flood of liquidations in the high-beta names we’re tracking. Instead, they're holding their ground. I’m staring at 40+ positions in our portfolio and not one of them is flashing the "get out" sign right now. That means the regime isn't push-your-chips-all-in bullish, but it’s also not sounding alarms for a full retreat either. Let’s call it what it is: indecision. A pit stop. And you know what happens after a pit stop? Someone punches the gas.

Right now, our existing positions are the real show. Coal ($BTU) continues to smolder, hitting our 2x target—chalk up another win for the contrarians betting on dirty energy. Speaking of resources, the Rare Earth ($UAMY, $MP) and Uranium plays ($UUUU, $SMR, $UEC) are looking like an underground revolution waiting to surface. Let's not forget Crypto, which is still quietly grinding higher with names like $ETHA, $BLSH, and $BMNR keeping the faith while $COIN flexes its strength post-2x.

If you’re late to the party, there might still be time to grab cocktails: $BTU has already served us two rounds at 2x but looks primed for more upside, while $MP is playing the pivot, ready to either consolidate or rip into uncharted territory. **Rare Earths are the cheat code no one’s talking about in this stagnant macro regime.** Meanwhile, keep an eye on energy names like $OXY and $APA. Yeah, they’re still digesting gains, but energy has shown leadership all year—and that’s not changing anytime soon.

Today, keep tabs on sectors that can snap out of this calm before the storm. Software is an ugly dog that might bark soon—$SE, $RZLV, and $SOUN have held steady despite zero squeeze action. That tells me something. And Asia? $NIO, $LI, and $GDS haven’t tapped out yet, even with all the noise about China. That resilience alone is a clue.

This quiet won’t last forever. Neutral regimes pivot hard, and when they do, they don’t look back. The moment the market decides where it wants to go, you won’t want to be late to the next rotation.
